Let's be real, most of the small culture wars that lead people away from Reddit to 'freer' horizons don't involve and probably never will involve the screenwriting subreddit. The screenwriting subreddit does a good, if imperfect, job and it's a fine community. This subverse is for the people who migrate from reddit and don't want to split their attention between Voat and reddit. Over the next few weeks, I'll try to post and flesh out ground rules and the like.

If you subscribe, let me know what you want to see here, etc and we'll make it happen.

What I would like to see are a wide variety of contests that users can submit content to. Things like: 10-page short film scripts, single page contests, best logline, maybe a monthly feature-length contest, etc...

Obviously the main bottleneck with these would be finding enough people willing to spend time judging these things, but if we're gonna dream big, that's what I'd like to see.
What would you suggest as a prize? I don't know if the subreddit is established enough to really warrant the idea just yet, but we could do something along the lines of flair or what-not.

I have a few thoughts, but I'm not sure how others would feel. The /r/screenwriting on reddit used to be one of my favorite places to go. Now, I don't like it so much. They used to have a simple flair system, and simple categories. In time, the flair got removed (now it's optional). And, the community used to be more welcoming to new writers. Now, it has a very different vibe of Blacklist submitters and WGA Screenwriters, and it makes me feel quite inferior. I'm more interested in a place where I can learn and discuss things. Some posts I see looking for feedback are completely ignored. As for me, I'm looking for 4 things:
- [CRITIQUE_ME] - where you can post your screenplay and request feedback
- [DISCUSS_PUBLISHED_SCREENPLAY] - where you can discuss something you've read online
- [ASK_QUESTION] - where you can ask a question
- [CONTEST] - where there are contests
Of course, there are better category names that could be chosen. These are just very blunt in order to describe their function.
In the subverse, I'd be very interested in collaboration and learning. I need to be held accountable. And, I find the best way to do that is to have a great, helpful community. Anyhoo, that's my two cents.

I've looked into making flair and it's currently unavailable for non-mods to add post flair. Saying that, I very much agree. Ask a question and discuss published screenplays are good categories that I hadn't thought of. Thanks.

I also feel the screenwriting subreddit's decision to flair users is something I'm personally against (I mean, a flaired user will huff 'you're wrong' even related to a non-business related comment and see soaring upvotes regardless of the truth of the post.) We'll do our best to not allow that sorta thing.

Hopefully, with the help of more posters/users, we can make this a better environment for writers.
